deck_name: 37 - Robotics Kinematics, ROS 2, CAN Bus & Motor Control

cards.prompt: What is the difference between Forward Kinematics (FK) and Inverse Kinematics (IK) in a robotic manipulator or 2-axis gimbal?
cards.answer: FK computes end-effector pose from joint angles; IK computes required joint angles from a target pose
accepted_answers: FK goes from joint angles to pose; IK goes from pose to joint angles
cards.explanation: Forward kinematics has a unique closed-form solution, whereas inverse kinematics can have multiple solutions, no solution (out of workspace), or singularities.

cards.prompt: What matrix relates joint velocities (q_dot) to end-effector linear and angular velocities (v) in robotics, and what happens when its determinant approaches zero?
cards.answer: The Jacobian matrix; the robot is at a kinematic singularity
cards.explanation: At a kinematic singularity (det(J) = 0), the manipulator loses one or more degrees of freedom and inverse velocity commands approach infinity.

cards.prompt: What underlying middleware standard does ROS 2 use for real-time node discovery and pub/sub data transport?
cards.explanation: ROS 2 replaces ROS 1's single-point-of-failure roscore master with decentralized DDS discovery and configurable QoS policies.

cards.prompt: In ROS 2, which communication primitive should you use for: (a) continuous 100 Hz IMU streams, (b) quick synchronous parameter/mode toggles, and (c) long-running trajectory execution with feedback and preemption?
cards.explanation: Topics handle unidirectional streaming, Services handle short request/response RPCs, and Actions handle preemptable long-running tasks with continuous feedback.

cards.prompt: In ROS 2 QoS settings, why is 'Best Effort' reliability preferred over 'Reliable' for high-rate camera frames or lidar scans over Wi-Fi?
cards.answer: It avoids retransmission stalls and head-of-line blocking when newer sensor frames arrive milliseconds later
accepted_answers: prevents retransmission latency on stale sensor data
cards.explanation: Retransmitting a dropped 30 Hz camera frame delays fresh frames; Best Effort drops stale packets to keep latency minimal.

cards.prompt: In CAN 2.0B, how is bus arbitration resolved when two nodes transmit simultaneously, and does a lower or higher 11-bit/29-bit ID win?
cards.answer: Non-destructive bitwise arbitration; the lower numeric ID wins
accepted_answers: bitwise arbitration where lower ID wins
cards.explanation: Dominant bits (0) overwrite recessive bits (1); a node transmitting 1 that reads back 0 backs off immediately without corrupting the winning frame.

cards.prompt: What are the maximum payload sizes (in bytes) of a Classic CAN 2.0 frame versus a CAN FD frame?
cards.answer: 8 bytes for Classic CAN 2.0, 64 bytes for CAN FD
cards.explanation: CAN FD extends payload capacity from 8 bytes up to 64 bytes and allows higher bitrates during the data phase.

cards.prompt: What file format defines CAN message IDs, DLC lengths, signal bit offsets, endianness, scaling factors, and physical units for embedded toolchains?
cards.explanation: A .dbc file acts as the single source of truth for encoding/decoding raw CAN payload bytes into physical engineering values.

cards.prompt: In a 3-phase BLDC motor controlled via Field-Oriented Control (FOC), what do the Clarke and Park transforms accomplish?
cards.answer: They transform 3-phase sinusoidal currents (abc) into a rotating 2-axis DC frame (d-q) aligned with the rotor flux
accepted_answers: convert 3-phase AC currents into rotating DC d-q frame
transform abc to rotating d-q coordinates
cards.explanation: In the rotating d-q frame, torque-producing current (Iq) and flux-producing current (Id) become constant DC quantities that standard PI controllers can regulate easily.

cards.prompt: Why must complementary high-side and low-side MOSFET gate signals in an H-bridge or 3-phase inverter include hardware 'dead-time'?
cards.answer: To prevent shoot-through (shorting Vbus directly to GND) while transistors turn off and on
accepted_answers: avoid shorting power to ground during switching
cards.explanation: MOSFETs take tens of nanoseconds to switch off; dead-time inserts a brief off-window so both transistors in a half-bridge are never conducting simultaneously.

cards.prompt: How does a quadrature rotary encoder (Channels A and B 90 degrees out of phase) determine direction of rotation and multiply resolution by 4x?
cards.answer: Direction comes from which channel leads; 4x resolution comes from counting both rising and falling edges of both A and B
accepted_answers: phase lead gives direction and counting all 4 edges gives 4x resolution
cards.explanation: Hardware timer encoder peripherals decode all four state transitions per quadrature cycle and automatically increment or decrement the counter register.

cards.explanation: Negative torque/duty commands are clamped to 0 before writing to the timer Capture/Compare Register (CCR), preventing unsigned underflow to 64286 (full throttle!).

cards.explanation: 0x01F4 in decimal is (1 * 256) + 244 = 500; multiplying by a .dbc scaling factor of 2 yields 1000 RPM.

cards.prompt: In a 2D differential-drive mobile robot with wheel radius R and wheelbase L, what happens physically when left and right wheel angular velocities are equal and opposite (w_R = -w_L)?
cards.answer: The robot rotates in place around its center (zero linear velocity)
cards.explanation: Linear velocity v = (R/2)*(w_R + w_L) = 0, while angular velocity omega = (R/L)*(w_R - w_L) != 0.

cards.prompt: Which standard ROS 2 package maintains the time-varying 3D coordinate frame tree (e.g., map -> odom -> base_link -> camera_link)?
cards.explanation: tf2 tracks relationships between coordinate frames over time and lets nodes transform sensor points from camera coordinates into robot base or world coordinates.
